documentation: bool applies Python’s truth-value rules. Empty built-in containers, zero, None and False are falsey. A nonempty string remains truthy even when its text looks like the word false.
caution: This is not a parser for textual Boolean labels. For example, bool("false") is True.
scenarios: Check whether a local result list has any items.
Choose a display fallback for an empty collection.
Convert a truth-test result into an explicit Boolean.
title: Apply Python truth-value rules
problem: Input is any JSON value. Return bool(input) using Python semantics. Empty lists and objects are falsey in Python, unlike JavaScript’s empty-array and empty-object truthiness.
goal: Use bool() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Call bool directly; do not parse the contents of a string.
